messages:
Marta L.: FYI — ECC error count just spiked across rack-7A. 6 cards with rising ECCs over the last 10m, plus repeated Xid 13s on a couple nodes. Possible bad batch or PCB issue. Attaching brief logs below.

Marta L.: ```
[2024-04-10 14:12:03] node=ip-10-1-7-22 gpu=0 serial=ABC12345 ECC_ERRS=142 XID=13 temp=71C
[2024-04-10 14:12:10] node=ip-10-1-7-22 gpu=1 serial=ABC12346 ECC_ERRS=129 XID=13 temp=70C
[2024-04-10 14:15:01] node=ip-10-1-7-45 gpu=2 serial=ABC98765 ECC_ERRS=99 XID=13 temp=69C
```

gpu-monitor-bot: Automated alert: ECC spike threshold breached on cluster-redwood-prod (rack-7A). Created alert INFRA-3241. Suggested action: cordon + drain affected nodes.

Alex P.: ok — before mass drains, can we confirm cross-rack correlation? query by serials and vendor lot. If it's a lot issue we should stop scheduling GPUs from that lot.

Ryan C.: ran a quick correlation: serials map to vendor lot L-2023-09-B2. Same lot showing elevated ECCs in rack-7A and a few cards in rack-9C. Thermal history shows extra thermal cycles on those hosts in the last 30d.

Devon (eng-infra): Proposed immediate playbook: 1) tag affected GPUs (quarantine), 2) cordon nodes, 3) run controlled drain of pods with GPU taint/eviction, 4) run full `nvidia-smi` health dump and collect HWM logs, 5) open RMA with vendor including serial list + HWM.

Devon (eng-infra): Example commands:```
# mark node so scheduler skips it
kubectl label node ip-10-1-7-22 gpu.quarantine=true
# cordon + drain (ignore daemonsets, gracefully evict GPUs)
kubectl cordon ip-10-1-7-22 && kubectl drain ip-10-1-7-22 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
# local health dump
sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,serial,ecc.errors,fan.speed,temperature.gpu --format=csv -f /tmp/gpu-health-$(hostname).csv
```

Marta L.: Sounds good. Can someone add a short-term alert tweak: ECC_ERRS > 50 in 5m -> P2, and slope > 10/min -> page. We're missing the slope indicator today.

Alex P.: I'll push a quick rev to monitoring. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/commit/abcd1234 — adds `increase(ecc_errors[5m]) > 10` rule and a dashboard panel for serial-level ECC trend.

gpu-monitor-bot: INFRA-3241 updated: status=investigating, assignee=Devon (eng-infra), linked_alerts=[ecc-spike-rack7]. RMA ticket draft created.

Ryan C.: note for postmortem: pattern looks like intermittent Xid 13 + ECC accumulation, not single catastrophic failure. Could be flaky VRAM modules on a vendor subset. Recommend capture of pre-failure KV cache states for any future incidents.

Devon (eng-infra): Action items agreed: 1) quarantine affected serials and stop scheduling new jobs on racks 7A/9C (immediately) 2) schedule maintenance window for physical inspection + RMA packing (tomorrow 22:00 UTC) 3) update runbook with drain steps + `nvidia-smi` dump file format 4) follow up postmortem next Wed (assign INFRA-3241). :thumbsup:

Marta L.: Thanks team — we'll treat this as recurring-failure candidate. Please add any additional serials you find to INFRA-3241 and include photos/RAIDs from onsite techs. We'll loop in vendor ops and legal if RMA volume looks large.

Alex P.: quick note — disable auto-scheduler placement for jobs with >2h runtime on those racks until RMA done. I'll flip the placement policy.

gpu-monitor-bot: note: temporary placement policy applied for cluster-redwood-prod — skip racks [7A,9C] for GPU jobs.

Marta L.: OK closing the thread for now, will start postmortem doc. If anyone observes Xid 31 or thermal trip, ping here immediately.
